text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: CUBISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Georges Braque

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A French artist born around 1880, Braque, along with Picasso, was the major exponent of Cubism, a new style of painting that fragmented and distorted the image in a radical way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although he began as a painter of landscapes and portraits, in 1911 Braque made a painting on which he pasted a piece of newspaper, Still Life with a Guitar.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It showed a table, a bottle and a guitar but treated all objects as if conventional perspective did not apply, representing them instead with flat planes, areas and shapes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The newspaper signified the presence of a newspaper in the still life, but was not a newspaper and did not look like one.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The act of sticking something onto the canvas initiated a revolution in painting, because it destroyed the integrity of the picture plane by acknowledging its physicality as a surface.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This had the effect of allowing a painting to be seen as an object as well as a flat representation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: No one had ever stuck anything onto a canvas to make part of the image before.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Braque’s achievement was to find a new way of representing form.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He began to include collage, using old tickets and printed paper (in one painting he uses paper printed with a rattan pattern to signify a cane chair), in another a piece of wood effect paper is used for a guitar for example.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made many such collages often depicting bottles, tabletops and wine glasses with the structural planes of the objects opened out and repositioned, before going on, as did Picasso, to attempt the same thing exclusively with paint.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Cubism was a way of representing all the planes of three dimensional objects on a two dimensional plane, to think of every object in terms of the surfaces of a series of cubes for the purposes of painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This way of looking at the physical world had been initiated by Cézanne.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Such a radical restructuring of pictorial space resulted in paintings made in browns and greys initially.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Braque sometimes used an elliptical canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The paintings gave the impression of crystalline forms with recognisable elements attached, such as a head, an eye, part of a guitar, the side of a bottle, the front of a table, the back of a chair.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Gradually Braque began to make a different kind of image becuase the effect of cubism had been to free the picture plane from the constraints of realistic representation and pictorial space.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The surface of the canvas became the pictorial space, so that the painting was both a representation and an exploration of surface.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Juan Gris

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A painter working at the same time and in a similar way to Braque.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is possible that Gris was the first to use collage on a painting, although Braque is given the credit for this.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Gris tended to make small paintings, sometimes using an oval format.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also went on to make Cubist paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Pablo Picasso

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Spanish artist Picasso is considered to be the greatest modern artist in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso’s work progressed through a number of different styles, including Cubism, and he made work in a variety of media.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His skill at drawing is consistently evident, but he was equally good at sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: From Picasso’s early career, his Blue period is the best known.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This describes a number of figurative paintings that have a blue light cast on them, for example a boy with a dove in his hand, and a young boy dressed as a Harlequin balancing on a ball.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The dove and the clown, particularly Harlequin and Pierrot, were recurring motifs throughout Picasso’s life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the early 1900s Picasso, along with Braque and Gris, would have seen African sculptures for the first time when a collection was exhibited in Paris.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This, combined with Cézanne’s experiments with the picture plane, led the three artists to make the first Cubist works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although Cubism is most readily attributed to Picasso, it was Gris who in fact made the first Cubist collage.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso made a number of these collages featuring bottles, guitars, as well as some small sculptures including one of a shelf with some domestic objects on it made from rough bits of wood and painted with a bobble braid tacked along the front.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso made a great number of Cubist paintings, which are rarely more than a metre high and predominantly brownish or greyish.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: During this period Picasso began to develop his mature style to reach its greatest achievement in two paintings, Guernica and Les Demoiselles D’Avignon.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Guernica was painted in 1917 to commemorate General Franco’s massacre of a Spanish village.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In it Picasso wanted to show the horror of war and suffering, and he was conscious of making a painting which would get attention.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made the painting immediately after the event and it was intended to be given to the town of Guernica.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is a very large painting, three meters by six, which shows a number of figures based clearly on African sculpture (for example Dogon masks) painted in black, purple, white and grey with everything outlined in black.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Guernica is an image of horror, of death and suffering, of weeping women, corpses and maimed bodies.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The limbs of the figures are intertwined so that the whole painting operates as an abstract composition as well.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was the first time a modern artist had made a painting that was such an explicit criticism of the government of the day.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Guernica was shocking and reproductions of the painting were instantly printed in newspapers all over the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Les Demoiselles D’Avignon is composed along similar lines but depicts a more pleasant scene of naked women in the countryside, painted in flesh tones and greens.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: However, the women have the same mask like faces as the figures in Guernica.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A film was made of Picasso making this painting, showing how he drew out the figures with continuous lines never once correcting himself or erasing anything.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso painted many portraits, often of the various women in his life, including Dora Maar, one of his lovers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These were never flattering, as the Cubist style which Picasso had made his own led to features being rearranged so that an eye might appear on the side of the head and the face be cut in two.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Black painted lines delineate everything and colour is entirely unrealistic.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso made a great deal of carved and assembled sculpture including a bull’s head made from a bicycle seat with a pair of handlebars for horns.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Drawing underpinned everything that Picasso did, and he made a large number of them, in particularly a number of black line drawings of the Minotaur, a myth which fascinated him.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Later in he made coloured lithographs that look like pastel drawings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These which are very well known, for example a simple hand holding a bunch of flowers and a dove with an olive branch in its beak.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In his exploration of every medium Picasso included ceramics, producing a great many plates, vases, and other objects, that he painted on and he also made a series of tooled and embossed silver platters.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Juan Miro

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picasso’s compatriot Miro took a very different route, making abstract paintings that drew on a variety of sources.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Miro uses amorphous shapes reminiscent of microscopic life forms that are painted on a thinly prepared raw linen ground.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Thin black lines and spidery nodes connect amorphous shapes in red and blue.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Miro borrowed compositional elements from comic strip drawings in particular the American Krazy Kat.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made collages using images cut from cutlery, tool and machinery catalogues that were often mixed with elements from cartoon strips and then abstracted to produce his paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In some ways Miro’s approach had an affinity with the work of the surrealists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Few artists have come close to achieving Picasso’s huge output in such a variety of media.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: But one French artist made paintings that were as influential as Picasso’s.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Henri Matisse

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matisse is considered one of the greatest artists in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His paintings include the famous Dance, an 8 metre by 3 metre panoramic painting of dancing female nudes, radical for its semi abstraction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The pink figures become rhythmic arabesques on the swirling blue ground.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matisse later made the figures into paper cut outs, a form in which he was prolific in later life, using ultramarine paper collaged onto a white ground.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: With the Snail, a large 4 by 3 metre collage made of a spiral of squares of different brightly coloured pieces of paper within a yellow collaged frame, these cut outs became Matisse's best known work, their graphic simplicity lending itself well to printed reproduction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The blue dancers, their heavy limbs creating a calligraphic pattern, are one of the most recognisable works by a twentieth century artist.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matisse also made a large number of drawings; he had an assured hand, creating very simple drawings often using one continuous line.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In his paintings it is Matisse’s use of drawing which sets his work apart.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He allowed a drawn edge to define the pictorial space and function both as part of an object or structure and part of the composition, and similarly he left areas of the canvas unpainted, allowing the white of the ground to function as part of the image.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matisse painted restful, joyous and domestic subjects in an entirely unsentimental, intellectual way.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His composition was daring, for example the Piano Lesson is a predominantly green and red painting composed of large blocks of colour, the entire painting bisected by a diagonal line, the head of a boy emerging from behind a piano very small in relation to the very large canvas.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The painting is figurative but it verges toward abstraction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is this abstract sensibility and his use of colour which singles Matisse out.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A head and shoulders portrait of a woman with a green face shows her with the shadow of her woman’s hat over her face painted in a swoop of emerald green.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matisse made literal translations of what his eye saw, so that if a shadow looked greenish, he painted it green, and if an edge could be made by not painting the canvas, he left it bare.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For example, another painting depicts a goldfish in a bowl on a table by a French window opening onto a tiny balcony.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The window and room are boldly outlined in black; the goldfish bowl and much else is half painted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Red Studio is a daring work, showing the furniture and objects in his studio outlined in white (made simply by leaving the canvas white where he wanted the line to be) and some colour, with minimal perspective, resulting in a painting that is a red square of canvas with objects, and some architectural elements such as a pair of shutters floating on it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Matisse also made a number of bronze casts, the best known of which is the triptych The Back, an abstracted human torso viewed from the back, carved in relief as semi cylindrical shapes to represent the two sides of the back and the buttocks, leaving a space in the middle to represent the division caused by the spine.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculptures were commissioned for a specific interior and were thus made as three bronze wall reliefs.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: At the turn of the century, the influence of photography on painting was clear.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It was also having an effect on sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This period saw some of the greatest sculptors emerge, leaving behind the tradition of copying classical sculpture and measuring from life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: EARLY TWENTIETH CENTURY SCULPTURE

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Auguste Rodin

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin, a French artist who is considered to be one of the greatest modern sculptors, made his best known works at the turn of the century.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Two of these, The Kiss (1901) and The Thinker are known all over the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin’s achievement was to use traditional stone and bronze cast sculpture techniques to represent movement, and to draw attention to the physical material property of the sculpture as a block of stone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin did not want to make sculpture that looked lifelike but was closer to the impressionists and cubists in his desire to acknowledge surface and material as an important part of the work for its own sake.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin saw the plinth as an integral part of the sculpture to be acknowledged rather than seen as an unfortunate necessity, again drawing attention to the sculpture as an object rather than something that should try to replicate reality.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He often left parts of the plinth unfinished or made his figures emerge from the stone of the plinth.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although Rodin was able to carve and model the human form with great accuracy he often exaggerated proportions to enhance the impression he wanted a particular work to make, using the tricks of classical sculpture such as perspective and foreshortening.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This can be seen very clearly in The Kiss, a white marble sculpture that shows a seated male and female nude entwined in a kiss.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The figures are about one and a half times larger than life, their bodies are carved without excess of detail, and the feet and legs are exaggerated.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The couple grow out of the stone block on which they sit which is left roughly carved.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Kiss has become a world famous representation of romantic and sexual love.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin made several copies and a number of smaller bronze versions.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There is a similar bronze of a girl lying on a low plinth, her body at points disappearing into the plinth as though it has not yet been formed.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In this work Rodin wanted to express the state of sleep.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin’s Thinker is an iconic work, a slightly larger than life size seated male nude with one elbow on a knee, the hand made into a fist on which the bent forward head rests.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculpture is made in bronze, with a very dark almost black patina and the modelling is relatively rough.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It grows out of a plinth about one metre high, raising the seated figure to the standing viewer’s eye level.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Thinker is a representation of existential angst, and gained its reputation by succeeding in the three dimensional representation of a state of mind.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is frequently reproduced, used in advertising or merely invoked in conversation by mimicking the physical gesture made by the figure.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This quotation of Rodin’s pose is both a reference to the actual sculpture and more generally to illustrate the idea of intense thought.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Walking Man is Rodin’s solution to another challenge – how to represent motion in figurative sculpture.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This is a life size dark brown bronze sculpture of a naked striding man who that on the floor on a minimal plinth so that the viewer is on the same level.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin made public commissions, the best known of which is The Burghers of Calais, which shows an event in French history in which the civic leaders of the town of Calais were imprisoned.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rodin’s sculpture shows them chained together, standing front to back and forming a melancholy circle, which draws the viewer to it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculpture itself forms a cage made by the bronze circle of figures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A statue of the French writer Balzac is a radical departure from contemporary portraiture – Balzac is shown standing, wrapped in a floor length cloak so that only his head is visible.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He has wild hair and a fierce expression and the figure leans back at an almost unrealistic angle.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A commission for a pair of monumental bronze gates for a public building in Paris resulted in The Gates of Hell, a bronze relief that occupied Rodin for years.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is a densely modelled depiction of purgatory covered with figures, for which Rodin did a large number of sketches and studies in bronze.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Constantin Brancusi

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another artist who considered the plinth to be a part of the sculpture was Brancusi, who lived and worked in Paris at the end of the 19th century.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Brancusi’s works were often no more than elaborated plinth shapes, with simple forms placed on them made in plaster, bronze, wood and marble.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of his best known works is Endless Column, a polished bronze column on a wooden plinth made of truncated three dimensional diamond shapes placed one on top of the other, about 10 metres high.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made a small carved head of a sleeping person which is so smooth and almost featureless as to almost appear to be a large stone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Alberto Giacommetti

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In contrast Italian artist Giacommetti had little interest in the plinth.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Giacommetti’s bronze sculptures are extremely elongated usually standing figures, sometimes single figures, sometimes pairs or groups which often imply movement, or seem to be about to walk.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They are solitary and isolated figures, reduced to essences of the human form.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculptures are not more than human height and often much smaller, the heads are tiny, the legs and arms no more than rods of metal, the bodies agglomerations of bronze that seem to serve merely to join the limbs, not much more than 30 cm wide.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The sculptures are modelled roughly so that the metal looks as if it has been dripped, dragged and pinched.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Giacommetti made a large number of working drawings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Gaudier Henri Brzeska

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Gaudier Brzeska made stone and bronze sculptures, mostly small and medium sized, for example a small dark stone carving of a curled up sleeping fawn.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For the first time artists were entirely free to make whatever they wanted, the only constraint being financial.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Photography began to be seen as part of an artist’s practise, abstraction was on the horizon, and the old traditions ceased to hold sway.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Several major movements carried art into the twentieth century and the period known as modernism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are surrealism, futurism and dada.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: SURREALISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Surrealist art was made in the context of the publishing of Freud’s work on the subconscious and of the liberation of art from straightforward narrative or representation of the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The subconscious mind offered new worlds to explore.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Salvador Dali

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This Spanish artist, born in 1900, is with Magritte the most famous of the surrealists and a candidate for best known artist in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Dali’s paintings or even details of his paintings are instantly recognisable such as the melted clocks which from a small part of one painting but which are instantly associated with Dali and surrealism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Dali’s surrealism is fantastical, he created dreamlike landscapes filled with distorted objects, nightmarish scenes and apocalyptic wastelands and religious iconography.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One painting shows mutant human bones that seem to have a life of their own in a grey green no man’s land, the aftermath of a war.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another shows the crucifixion from Christ’s point of view, showing what he would have seen looking down from the cross, the whole image a luridly coloured hallucination.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A landscape with dead trees has clock faces draped on the trees and on the ground apparently melting and dripping.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A giant red rose floats in the air above a desert.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A telephone receiver is replaced by a lobster.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Where Dali’s use of obvious symbolism and his lurid hallucinatory images have made him enduringly popular, his personal eccentricity has only increased his popularity and is difficult to separate from his work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Dali dressed as a dandy, often wearing white and sporting a very long waxed moustache that extended beyond his face and pointed up.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He lived with his wife Galia in a house in Spain at Figuera da Foz where the couple were host to many of their contemporaries.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Dali is not considered to be the intellectual force behind surrealism, however well known his work has become.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This role is given to Breton.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Andre Breton

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The most outspoken member and leader of the surrealists in Paris at the beginning of the twentieth century, Breton made paintings and sculpture, and wrote the Surrealist manifesto that set out to define a new kind of art for new times.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His best known work is a clothes iron with spikes set into the sole plate.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Rene Magritte

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Magritte is the most famous of the Surrealists, and indeed is one of the best known artists in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A French painter born in 1850, Magritte’s images are instantly recognisable and attributable, and have been much copied.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They have influenced advertising imagery for several decades and continue to do so.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Magritte was interested in both visual and textual puns, for example, ‘Ceci n’est pas une pipe’ (this is not a pipe) is inscribed on a painting of a pipe.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Many of his paintings feature both words and objects and often the objects are apparently named but the names do not make sense.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In this way Magritte's text paintings are both object and subject in the sense that are what they are but the viewer is then told that they are not, leading them to a new consideration of what they are seeing and of what art might do.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Many of Magritte's paintings are very well known: a train emerging from a fireplace; an apple obscuring most of the front of a bowler hatted man’s face; an inverted mermaid with a fish’s head and woman’s legs and pelvis; an easel by a window with a painting on it, the painting showing the view through the window; two grey spaceship like objects titled Floating Spheres; and a man’s face which is also a female torso in which the pubic hair is also the man’s beard.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These are painted in a highly realistic but flat and stiff style, with a muted palette, smooth, flat and few brushstrokes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The ludicrous juxtapositions of objects and people are nonetheless poetic and leave the viewer hoping that they might actually happen, that the everyday might mix up and become magical, in other words, surreal.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Man Ray

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A French surrealist sculptor, painter and photographer working in Paris in the early twentieth century, Man Ray experimented with photography to create unique images, using various methods including placing objects on light sensitive plates and then exposing them to get an image.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Man Ray took a well known photograph of Duchamp with a star shaved out of the back of his head smoking a pipe.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Meret Oppenheim

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Oppenheim made a sculpture of a fur covered cup, saucer and spoon, as well as one of a pair of white high heeled shoes upside down on a silver salver trussed with string and paper frills on the ends of the heels.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: She also made a pair of leather gloves, the conventional stitched ridges on the backs of each made to resemble the veins on the back of a hand.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Hans Bellmer

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Bellmer made photographs of dolls and parts of dolls arranged in tableaux, as well as sculptures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His work deals with sexual taboo.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Lazlo Moholy Nagy

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This Hungarian artist was a contemporary of the surrealists and is best known for a number of pioneering semi abstract films and photographs using architectural form, light and shade.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Surrealism provided the context for an avant garde group of artists, performers and writers to produce work that they collectively titled Dada.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: DADA

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The dada artists were based in Berlin but drawn from a number of different nationalities.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They worked in all media and also made performance and musical work, performing regularly under the name Cabaret Voltaire.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The name comes is a combination of a French word for hobby horse but was intended to have no specific meaning.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Marcel Duchamp

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Known in the twentieth century as the father of conceptualism, the French artist Marcel Duchamp was among the artists escaping Europe for America to avoid censorship and persecution as Jews.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He founded Dada and became notorious for his controversial and usually sculptural works, in particular the ones that became known as ready mades.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The notorious Fountain, exhibited at the Armoury show in New York in 1913 was in fact a gents’ ceramic urinal placed on its sided so that it could be said to have the shape of a Buddha or a wall fountain.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Duchamp signed the urinal on the front, R.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Mutt, (one of the invented punning names that Duchamp used to sign his work).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Fountain created a furore because it was a bought object, to which nothing had been added, that Duchamp claimed to make into a work of art merely by the act of signing it and proclaiming authorship.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The radical step taken by Duchamp with his ready mades, a cycle wheel attached to the seat of a stool for example or a metal bottle dryer, was to have far reaching implications for art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Duchamp employed pseudonyms and puns as part of his work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He created a female alter ego, Rrose Selavy (a pun on ‘C’est la vie’), who authenticated and signed many of his works including the urinal.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He photographed himself dressed as Rrose, a rather unconvincing manifestation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Rrose produced a perfume named La Belle Haleine, literally ‘beautiful breath’, intended as an allusion to its opposite, bad breath, and a pun on ‘La belle Helene’, Helen of troy.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Inframince or infrathin was a concept involving the declaration of an invisible or intangible and banal act or action to be a work of art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: For example the static friction and the sound of velvet trouser legs rubbing together and the warmth left on a recently vacated seat.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Almost as notorious as Fountain was Duchamp’s defaced reproduction of the Mona Lisa.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Making a pun on the letters LHGC which appear below the face of the Mona Lisa he wrote that ‘elle a un grand cou’ which translates as ‘she has a fat arse’ and drew a moustache on her face.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This re appropriated image became one of the best known images in twentieth century art.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Duchamp made a number of bronze and wax sculptures which were casts of male and female sexual parts, taking, for example, a mould from female genitals which gave him a negative from which he cast in bronze rather than make a positive from it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of Duchamp's last works was L’Origin du Monde, a large peepshow containing a wax female torso, laid on an apparent mossy bank, the head out of view, with the genitals exposed.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There is a drawing by Courbet of a nude in a similar pose.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The apparently innocent tableau with its celebratory title became due to the voyeuristic way in which the viewer was required to look at it tainted with an atmosphere of illicit pleasure, abuse or even murder.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Large Glass, also known as The Bride Stripped Bare by her Bachelors Even, is a large sculpture comprising a screen print onto two pieces of glass held in a metal freestanding frame which was made in an edition.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This is Duchamp’s least understood work and it has always resisted interpretation.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The images printed on the glass are geometric rays, lines and a coffee grinder with three buckets that was a motif Duchamp repeatedly returned to and had made several drawings of.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The buckets on the grinder are sometimes supposed to represent the bachelors, but in general the meaning of the work remains opaque.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Duchamp also made several paintings of the coffee grinder that appears in the Large Glass.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Duchamp was photographed by Man Ray with a star shaved out of the back of his close cut hair.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He played chess every day of his life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Kurt Schwitters

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schwitters, a leading Dada artist and poet, invented the concept of Merz, a way of working and making art that he applied to everything he did.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The most significant manifestation of this is the Merzbau, the interior of a house of which he transformed in its entirety by constructing organic and crystalline protrusions and projections from timber, wire, plaster and papier maché.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The rooms became like white caves or cubist grottos.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schwitters also made the (unfinished) Merzbarn during the time he spent in the Lake District in England, a small stone cottage that he transformed with cement and plaster reliefs.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schwitters began his career as a graphic designer and typographer and produced innovative work using unusual combinations of typefaces.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He developed an interest in type as a visual form and much of his later work incorporates type in the form of cut out and collaged letters and drawn text.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schwitters wrote poetry, which he performed at Dada performances and at Cabaret Voltaire.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His tone poems consisted mainly of sound rather than words.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The best known is titled Caravane, which Schwitters intoned through a megaphone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He regarded his poems as aural images.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schweitzer’s small collages are made from coloured paper, printed paper, cut out printed letters, found images, drawing, paint and other materials.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a great number of these, mostly postcard sized which just predate Braque’s and Gris’s use of collaged text as part of an image.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schwitters also made three dimensional objects, reliefs and assemblages from found materials, timber, wire and paint.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Johannes Baader

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Baader was a German artist involved in Dada and Cabaret Voltaire performances.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Baader also worked on his own and carried out a number of extreme public performances, often involving physical risk to himself.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a lot of pamphlets and distributed them in mass public leafleting actions for which he was frequently arrested.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Hugo Ball

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Ball was a leading Dada performance artist and a prominent member of Cabaret Voltaire, instigating many of the collaborative performances and writing many of the poems and scripts for them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Luigi Russolo

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Art of Noise, Russolo’s orchestra, played at many Cabaret Voltaire performances.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Russolo was an experimental musician and composer; there were no conventional instruments in his orchestra, which consisted of household appliances and especially made instruments often producing a deliberate cacophony.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Italy produced an avant garde at the turn of the century which bears comparison with Dada but had entirely different stated aims.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There had been no Italian surrealism but de Chirico’s painting presented a reflexive view of Italian culture and civic life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Giorgio De Chirico

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The towns and architecture depicted in de Chirico’s work are very distinctive for their deserted atmosphere, as if time stands still and the buildings cast long shadows in a strong sunny light.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One painting of an empty town square has a statue of an unspecified man, a tower and an arched arcade or cloister.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The shadows cast by the buildings and statue on the yellow ochre ground and under the arcade are black.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another painting has the fallen head of a classical marble statue, very like Michelangelo’s David, seen lying on its side on the ground, with a broken off hand in the background, offering a critique of Italy’s reliance on the culture of its past rather than of the present.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: FUTURISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In this environment of stultification and Mussolini’s dictatorship, the Futurists, who were based in Milan, wrote a manifesto declaring that speed was their god and that the Future was the only thing worth making art about.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They were reflecting the times, in a period when manufacturing design was changing rapidly, people and news could travel fast, and moving pictures were available to entertain everyone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Frederico Marinetti

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The leading member of the Italian Futurist movement, Marinetti was an eccentric didactic who produced many paintings and published texts include several versions of the Futurist Manifesto.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He wrote a Futurist Cookbook, in which he declared pasta to be the most important (and futurist) of all food.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The book contains many edible recipes including several for pasta, but also some very inedible and often ironic ones involving rose petals and entirely green banquets, for example, with complicated presentation methods.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It offers a glimpse into the surprising romanticism of the futuristic movement.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Marinetti made several performance works including one in which a set of dining chairs were made to dance on and off the stage.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Giacomo Balla

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Balla pursued an obsession with speed in his paintings, trying to find the ultimate way to depict people, animals and objects in motion.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A portrait of a dachshund walking with spoke like lines emanating from each of its legs is one example.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Umberto Boccioni

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Boccioni is considered to be the best futurist painter and sculptor, much of his work dealing with how to represent speed in two or three dimensions.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A bronze sculpture about one metre high called simply ‘Speed’ depicts a striding man, with apparently aerodynamic fin like structures representing trails of movement leading backwards from his limbs and the back of his head.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The streamlined helmet shape of his head and the armour like fins give the sculpture a sinister warrior like quality.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Boccioni made a head of Mussolini by drawing a profile copied from a photograph and using this as a guide to a piece of wood.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The result is a solid object which has the shape of a vase but the unmistakeable profile of a man from whichever angle it is regarded.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He also made many paintings of his native Milan usually with lines radiating to represent movement of people and vehicles.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Frances Picabia

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picabia’s work did not follow Futurist prescription but he did have an interest in technological development.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picabia’s work does not fit into any movement but he was very influential and is best known for paintings that depict human machine like figures, abstract paintings and his use of text.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Picabia also worked as a graphic designer and designed typefaces.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Tamara de Lempicka

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In France, Lempicka painted the newly liberated women of the time.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Lempicka appears in her own work, distinctive for her straight bobbed hair with low fringe and fashionable clothes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the early twentieth century many artists made work that depicted a futuristic world, either utopian or dystopian.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some reflected on the increasingly urban, industrialised way of life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Fernand Léger

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Léger, a French painter, had a distinctive style, painting figures as if their bodies were composed of tubular elements, in shaded greys on a whiter ground with occasional additions of primary colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Léger’s figures look like metal puppets or robots.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Other artists concentrated on the traditional forms of portraiture and still life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ernesto Modigliani

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The name Modigliani is always associated with a certain type of portrait, typically of a seated woman with an elongated body and stylised face.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Modigliani's portraits are contemplative and painted in a sombre palette with black outlines.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Giorgio Morandi

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Most of Morandi’s still life paintings depict the simplified forms of domestic objects such as jugs, bottles and vases on plain coloured grounds.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Nicholas De Stael

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: De Stael also painted simple still lifes using flat bright colours.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: EARLY PHOTOGRAPHY

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The work of American photographers in the first few decades of the twentieth century was very influential.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: They recorded both the social conditions of the depression and the opening up of the vast landscapes of the west.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Among them were Edward Weston and William Egglestone who photographed city life.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Walker Evans

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Evans took photographs of rural America during the thirties Depression that showed the extreme poverty and suffering of ordinary people.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ansel Adams

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Adams was a pioneer of landscape photography known chiefly for his images of American national parks and wildernesses, such as Yosemite and Yellowstone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: When he made these photographs the wildernesses were not well explored and many parts were remote and inaccessible, necessitating many days trekking with equipment to get the images he wanted.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The photographs capture the enormity and grandiosity of the landscape and came to represent the American wilderness to the rest of the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Because of their huge scope and precise depth of field they seem to be photographic records of time passing, although of course they only record a moment in time.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: An example is a photograph of the central valley in Yosemite which shows a huge waterfall cascading down the opposite side of the valley.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Europe, photographers like Eugene Atget and Bill Brandt were recording events, and Brassai was beginning to make abstract images.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Andresz Kertesz

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Eastern European photographer Kertesz made images that became instantly familiar, including one of the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Seen from a bird’s eye view there is snow on the road surface and the tracks of the few vehicles on the streets have inscribed black parabolas around the arch on the white ground.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Claude Cahun

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Cahun was a French photographer who made a number of self portraits in which she is dressed as a man without disguising her sexual identity.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: THE MOVING IMAGE

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artists were trying to represent movement in different ways.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Futurists wanted to represent speed and Rodin to create a sculpture of the human form that conveyed movement.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The invention of moving pictures was less of an early influence on them than the work of one photographer.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Eadweard Muybridge

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: At the turn of the century, Muybridge, an American photographer, made a series of photographs of a horse and a man in motion.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He took a series of exposures at close intervals, producing an image for every second of movement.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The resulting images had a great influence on artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Muybridge's sequential exposures showed a specific action, for example the components of the movement of a naked walking man and of a galloping horse.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In the days before moving pictures, no one had foreseen that movement could be represented photographically, reduced to a sequence of still images, nor had they been able to study movement.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Design and architecture were changing rapidly in Europe and America as a new style emerged, known as International Modernism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was a sleek, unadorned way of building championed by Le Corbusier among others.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Modernist architects were, like the futurists, enthusiastic about the future, proclaiming that in the future everybody would have a home of their own, a modular unit or machine for living in.
