text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Design schools were established to train a new breed of architects and designers.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Bauhaus and De Stijl are the best known.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: THE BAUHAUS

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Bauhaus was in Berlin and was a multi disciplinary school with a distinct ethos.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Students studied across all areas, including theatre design, textiles, ceramics and graphics, as well as architecture and industrial design.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some Bauhaus students went on to become artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Oskar Schlemmer

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Schlemmer studied at the Bauhaus as a theatre designer and he made a number of sculptural designs for the Bauhaus productions, later becoming an artist.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: De Stijl was the Dutch design school at which Gerrit Reitveld, the designer of the famous Red Blue Yellow chair, studied.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The influence of the painter Mondrian and Russian constructivism can clearly be seen in De Stijl design.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Piet Mondrian

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Mondrian was a Dutch artist who began by painting his local countryside, trees and canals before abstracting these scenes and simplifying his palette.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Mondrian also experimented with canvas shape, making a series of abstract works on oval canvases that were based on trees in a snowy landscape.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These were conveyed as geometric grey and brown marks on a white ground and Cézanne was influenced by them.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Mondrian made a series of works on small square canvases painted on a white ground, dividing the canvas into irregular blocks with black horizontal and vertical lines and colouring in some of the resulting squares and rectangles with red, yellow and blue.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: These works are amongst the most famous abstract paintings in the world.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Later Mondrian began to paint patterns using smaller units and areas, for example Who’s Afraid of Red, Yellow and Blue? in 1910, and one titled Subway, which are an homage to the architecture and the new jazz scene of New York.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Mondrian's abstract geometric compositions owe something to contemporary Russian constructivists but are significant for their abstraction of landscape into pure geometric form.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: CONSTRUCTIVISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In Russia, artists began to make paintings and sculpture that were based on architectural form.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This was a reaction to the prevailing socialist realist art sponsored by the state, which often amounted to little more than Soviet propaganda.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Art served the state by representing rural agricultural life as idyllic but productive, and portrayed the worker as the hero of the day.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artists rebelled by finding a way of working that was entirely different, and most importantly, abstract.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Vladimir Tatlin made his spiral staircase monument.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Constructivism used geometry, sharp edged straight lines and primary colours, and the artists laid down the principles on which works could be made.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It had a great influence on contemporary graphic design and typography, and continued to do so throughout the twentieth century.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Constructivism was later taken up by Europeans such as the French painter Victor Vasarely.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: SUPREMATISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Kasimir Malevich

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A Russian artist called Malevich developed a form of constructivism that he named suprematism and made primary coloured paintings on white grounds.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He painted the famous Black Square in 1910.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This work was the logical if daring conclusion of his systematic attention to constructivist principles and is often attributed with marking the beginning of abstraction.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: It is also a stark political statement that there is nothing left to paint.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Black square is simply a square canvas painted black all over.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Square canvases were very unusual since they did not lend themselves well to the composition of traditional subjects of painting, landscapes and portraits.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The square drew attention to the work itself, not the subject of the work, so that the painting became an object about painting rather than a depiction of something became important.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Mondrian soon began to use the square format.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Malevich's painting was entirely black which drew attention to the only possible details of his work, the colour of the black and the brushstrokes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The viewer was directed to regard only the physicality of the paint in this work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This may have been more than Malevich intended.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Wassily Kandinsky

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Another Russian artist, Kandinsky, is also credited with making some of the first abstract paintings.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Whereas Malevich had made a minimal painting, Kandinsky used bright colours and black on a white ground to make expressive gestural flowing marks, giving rise to the term abstract expressionism.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was interested in the relation of music to sound and some of his paintings are attempts to ‘paint’ music.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He painted some stage backdrops for experimental orchestral works.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.3; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.508

g.text:soa: GERMAN EXPRESSIONISM

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kirchner was an early German expressionist painter.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His paintings are brightly coloured, with angular stylised figures, and lots of brushstrokes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Kirchner was the founder of an artists’ group called die Brucke (The Bridge), which included Kandinsky among its members.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Die Brucke published a magazine of critical texts called Die Blaue Reiter (The Blue Rider).

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The First World War had a profound effect on artists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Oscar Kokoschka, Otto Mueller and others registered their horror at what had happened in their work.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Max Beckman

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beckman was a German artist who painted in an expressionist style, choosing to portray the people and social spaces of the day in Berlin.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A self portrait shows him full length, standing glaring at the viewer while wearing a large black overcoat and a hat with a wide brim.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Beckman used a lot of black to outline his figures.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Otto Dix

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Dix painted the First World War atrocities, including limbless and horrifically injured soldiers, the best known showing two veterans sitting at a café table, one of whom has had his leg blown off, the other has an eyeball hanging out.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: George Grosz

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Grosz painted the decadence of the Weimar republic at the beginning of the twentieth century and the aftermath of war.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Paul Nash

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of the few British artists who made paintings about the war, Nash showed barren landscapes of the trenches and no mans’ land in a slightly surrealist light, favouring greens and browns and populating his landscapes with skeletal shapes to create an atmosphere of death.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Egon Schiele

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Although Schiele did not directly paint about the war, his paintings are uneasy and cheerless portraits that were in tune with the times.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The young women and men in Schiele’s work are usually emaciated and have hollow faces and large eyes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His portraits usually show the whole body, sometimes more than one figure, usually naked or semi clothed on pale backgrounds and they are painted with rough brushstrokes and a palette of white with brown, grey and black.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Throughout the early twentieth century there were plenty of artists who ignored political events and continued to make art that represented romantic, spiritual or domestic subjects.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Balthus

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Balthus is renowned for his domestic interiors and the dreamlike quality of his paintings of young women and girls.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used a restrained palette and the features of his female sitters are flattened and idealised.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Balthus continued to paint until he was a very old man.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Marc Chagall

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Chagall is a French painter who also designed stained glass.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He is usually associated with images of lovers and animals who are sometimes flying.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His narrative paintings are executed in a faux naïve style, with soft colours and a sentimental quality.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Chagall often painted images of love and marriage, for example one painting shows a bride and groom resting on a giant hen in the sky, with symbols of the artist’s Jewish faith in the background.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As well as hens and roosters, Chagall liked to paint horses, for example one painting features a white horse with large green eyes and long eyelashes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Chagall was commissioned to design the stained glass windows for a chapel designed by le Corbusier in the south of France.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Raoul Dufy

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Known for his idyllic seaside scenes, Dufy used bright colours and quick gestural brushstrokes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was commissioned to paint a mural for the head quarters of the national French electricity generating company celebrating the benefits of electric power.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He made a large curved panorama showing people going about varying activities in the countryside, the city and at the seaside with electricity pylons linking the different scenes.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Robert Delaunay

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Delaunay made semi abstract paintings using bright, luminous colours, usually in small squares.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He was married to Sonia Delaunay.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Sonia Delaunay

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: As well as making light bright coloured semi abstract paintings, Delaunay is known for her designs for woven and printed textiles.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Jean Arp

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Arp was a Dutch artist who worked in mixed media and painting, making a lot of wall hung reliefs and constructions using primary colours and white, and simple shapes, usually curved.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Arp cut out simple shapes from sheets of timber and glued them to a board, adding other elements and painting the whole thing.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Kees Van Dongen

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Van Dongen made semi abstract colourful paintings, applying the paint quite thickly.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Nolde and Munch made a new kind of expressionistic landscape painting.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Emile Nolde

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The Belgian artist Nolde's expressionistic landscapes and portraits are characterised by very bright colours and impasto.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Edvard Munch

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: One of the most famous modern paintings, The Scream, was painted by the Norwegian artist Munch.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: This iconic painting has often been used in advertising and has been stolen several times.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Munch had a very distinctive painting style, which gives the appearance of a woodcut at times.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He outlined his figures, often painting the background to follow the contours of the person in the painting to add to the outlining.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He used strong and often acidic colours in later works, but many of his earlier landscapes use soft colours and monochrome.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In The Scream, Munch wanted to suggest both the sound of the scream and the emotion that engendered it.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The figure of a screaming person dressed in black, with shocked eyes and hands to open mouth, is seen on a jetty, surrounded by concentric lines of bright colours that seem to represent the sound of the scream.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Munch's subjects were either the rural Norwegian landscape or people.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: There is often a dreamlike quality to his work, as if nothing were quite real; the sun is often a strange colour, shadows are distorted, and elements are coloured unnaturally.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The people in Munch’s work always seem to be or to feel that they are alone.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: A painting of a lake has a setting sun, the reflection of which is a thickly applied vertical yellow stripe on the water.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: In a lithograph called The Singer a woman dressed in black stands in a room with a piano.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The only bright colour in the painting is in the woman’s red hair.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: At the time The Scream was painted Freud’s theories of hysteria and the unconscious were just becoming known and also influenced the work of the surrealists.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some artists experimented more literally with the subconscious mind.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Henri Michaux

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Michaux was a French artist who made small obsessive drawings and written works, dense with scribbling, extremely intricate patterns and landscapes and letters to anonymous recipients written in the smallest of hands, sometimes blanked out after writing.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Michaux mainly used pen and ink, often brown ink, and made his drawings under the influence of mescaline, which Michaux believed allowed him fuller access to his subconscious.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: MC Escher

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The German artist Escher made extremely detailed and precise drawings of fantasy interiors and architecture, using impossible perspective or optical tricks thereby making something appear to change from convex to concave continuously.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: His work has been frequently reproduced, for example an interior with a staircase descending around four walls that never goes anywhere, a pattern of black and white doves that becomes something else, and a hand drawing itself which becomes a hand drawing itself.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The endgame of Esher’s work is characteristic, everything appears to return to itself.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Some artists made work in a naïve or faux naïve style.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Paul Klee

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The French painter Klee made a large number of small paintings and an enormous range of works on paper, using both drawing and printmaking.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Klee habitually used thin drawn lines to make geometric patterns, often repeated triangles or squares with dots, which were coloured and often resemble patchwork.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Sometimes these remained as abstract patterns, at other times Klee would draw figures, trees, buildings or animals.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Jan Dubuffet

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Dubuffet used sand to roughen the texture of his paint.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: He painted large simple figures and faces which owed something to African art but also to graffiti.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.2; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.392

g.text:soa: Auguste Maillol

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Maillol's bronze and stone sculptures have solid and rounded forms, as if they cannot escape from the block from which they are carved.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The bodies are distinctively simply formed, and even the smaller works have a gentle monumental quality.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: Artists’ groups were sometimes centred on a particular location.

text:soa.style: font-family: pm; font-size:1.1; text-rendering: optimizeLegibility; text-align: justify;line-interval:1.276

g.text:soa: The St Ives group is named after a town in the southwest of England to which they migrated to avoid the Blitz and because the quality of light was very good for painting.
